dedupe_keys.name: multi agent stochastic crew restoration model for power distribution systems coupled with the transportation network ieee 8500 node feeder and dallas fort worth tornado case

description: This record describes a stochastic two-stage mixed-integer programming framework for proactive crew allocation, assignment and routing in power distribution restoration after extreme events such as tornadoes, presented in an arXiv paper (version 2 of October 2025) by researchers at the University of Texas at Dallas and the University at Buffalo. The framework treats multiple repair crews as distinct agents for decentralised coordination, and models the interdependency between the power and transportation networks under uncertainty, since existing methods rely on deterministic heuristics or simplified models. The objective is to minimise service downtime and enhance restoration by coordinating repair operations. The case study uses the IEEE 8500-node test feeder integrated with a real transportation network from the Dallas-Fort Worth region, with tornado event data used to build failure scenarios of damaged grid components and transportation links. Results show more coordinated and efficient restoration strategies. Access: the paper on arXiv, free; no code or licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: an optimisation study on one feeder and region. It suits restoration planning research, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
